$about: The growing season average temperatures (°C) in which each grape makes its classic wine, read off Jones's climate-maturity chart (bars measured against its 13 to 21 °C axis, so about ±0.1 °C). The Atlas uses them to say which grapes a place's climate suits.

source.name: Jones, G.V. 2010, Climate, grapes, and wine: structure and suitability in a variable and changing climate, VIII International Terroir Congress, Figure 2 (after Jones 2006)

winkler.$about: Winkler regions by degree days above 10 °C (50 °F), April to October in the north and October to April in the south, with what each region suits, paraphrased from Wikipedia's table (General ripening capability and wine style).
regions: Only very early grapes ripen well, mostly hybrids and a few vinifera.
Early and mid-season grapes make good wine.
Good for generous crops of standard to good wine.
Big crops are possible, but quality tops out at acceptable.
Best for big crops of everyday wine, or table grapes.
